Security

The math keeps the promise.

Security claims on this page are scoped to named implementations and evidence. Browser self-tests demonstrate primitives, not every daemon path, deployment, endpoint, or provider boundary.

What we collect

No application signup or advertising profile.

The site avoids account identifiers, ad analytics, tracking pixels, fingerprinting code, and third-party browser scripts. Cloudflare and GitHub still receive ordinary request metadata, and website services process the fields listed on /transparency/.

The project does not maintain a conventional user or social-graph database, but it cannot claim identification is impossible: infrastructure providers, relays, endpoints, recipients, and network observers may retain or infer metadata.

Defends against

Current evidence, demonstrations, and capability requirements.

Passive eavesdropping.

/api/session advertises an ephemeral Worker X25519 public key while its ML-KEM-768 public key is null and pending. It performs no client ECDH or ML-KEM-768 exchange and therefore establishes no secure or PQ-protected browser-to-Worker session. Local primitive self-tests do not change that boundary.

Active impersonation.

A correctly completed two-device SAS comparison can expose an active substitution attempt. The same-tab website self-test does not provide that human, camera, transport, or second-device assurance.

Server compromise.

The design keeps plaintext off correctly implemented relays. Relay and /share/ services may hold ciphertext temporarily, and compromise can expose encrypted payloads plus routing, timing, size, session, and connection metadata.

Traffic analysis (in flight, lands v0.22)

Three-hop Sphinx logic is available as a local primitive demonstration, but daemon transport wiring and website traffic do not currently provide the advertised private route. Multi-hop routing reduces some single-relay visibility; it does not guarantee anonymity.

Lost device.

Local browser/WASM demonstration only. It does not prove released daemon integration, real-device recovery, persistent hardware protection, or every message path. Broader behavior remains a capability requirement until a versioned acceptance test is published.

Coerced unlock (in flight, lands v0.22)

Local browser/WASM demonstration only. It does not prove released daemon integration, real-device recovery, persistent hardware protection, or every message path. Broader behavior remains a capability requirement until a versioned acceptance test is published.

Where the trust is yours

Where the math hands off to you.

Honest about where the protocol ends and your judgment begins.

The physical space around you.

The protocol secures what travels across the wire. The screen in front of you is yours to guard, the same way it is for any conversation in any room.

Artifact signature

No One Link release signature, Windows Authenticode signature, or Apple Developer ID notarization is published for the rolling builds.

The people you choose to share with.

Implemented end-to-end-encrypted paths encrypt content before transport. Endpoints decrypt it; relay and website services may process ciphertext plus routing, timing, size, session, and connection metadata. Demo-only and capability-dependent paths are listed separately. Dots use random, rotating per-tab IDs that are pseudonymous to other visitors, not anonymous to infrastructure. Cloudflare receives ordinary connection metadata and the selected peer can retain anything received.

The widest of network-watchers.

Three-hop Sphinx logic is available as a local primitive demonstration, but daemon transport wiring and website traffic do not currently provide the advertised private route. Multi-hop routing reduces some single-relay visibility; it does not guarantee anonymity.

Evidence pointers; not proof of every claim.

Formal verification

Contributor-reported internal evidence only. No independent audit, version-pinned artifact, exact current command transcript, or external reproduction is published here; formal-verification, timing, and fuzz assertions remain requirements pending that evidence.

Constant-time crypto

Contributor-reported internal evidence only. No independent audit, version-pinned artifact, exact current command transcript, or external reproduction is published here; formal-verification, timing, and fuzz assertions remain requirements pending that evidence.

Fuzz testing

Contributor-reported internal evidence only. No independent audit, version-pinned artifact, exact current command transcript, or external reproduction is published here; formal-verification, timing, and fuzz assertions remain requirements pending that evidence.

Reproducibility and provenance

No byte-for-byte reproducibility result or artifact-bound build attestation is published for the rolling builds.

Experimental update check; publisher authentication pending.

Local hashing; rolling updates are not authenticated. A same-channel checksum can detect corruption but does not prove publisher identity. Current rolling artifacts have no published artifact signature or independent reproducibility result.

Verify the daemon you already have

The command produces a local install fingerprint for comparison. It is tamper evidence only when compared with a separately authenticated baseline; comparison with another unauthenticated download does not prove provenance.

Prove the bytes you're reading

Verify this site, in your tab.

The verifier authenticates the website-asset manifest with the offline site-manifest key and then re-hashes every listed file. The checked-in manifest is stale after the current website changes, so the full check fails and no current bundle-integrity verdict is published. This mechanism never authenticates application installers or proves a reproducible release build.

      Threshold recovery
      
Split a secret across five hands. Recover from any three.

      

        One click runs ol_threshold_recovery (Shamir secret sharing over GF(2^8), same crate the daemon uses). Your browser splits a 32-byte secret into 5 shares, then recovers it from any 3, and proves that any 2 cannot. The shares look random because they are random. The secret only exists when 3 of them come together.

      Coordinated vulnerability disclosure
      
Report privately; read the current commitments literally.

      
The contributor-run inbox below is the published reporting path. It is monitored on a best-effort basis, not by a staffed 24/7 security team. Response, remediation, CVE, credit, bounty, safe-harbor, and disclosure dates are not guaranteed. The targets below preserve the program we want to build without presenting it as operating capacity today.

      

        
Published reporting path
Email weareone@oneunity.earth with subject "security report". /.well-known/security.txt repeats this contact. Do not send exploit material or third-party personal data until scope and a protected exchange method are agreed. /share/ is a temporary browser-sharing demo, not an authenticated security-report channel.

        
Response targets; no SLA
Current status: contributor-run, with no guaranteed acknowledgement, triage, fix, or disclosure deadline. Non-guaranteed targets are acknowledgement within 72 hours, initial triage within 7 calendar days, and a mutually coordinated disclosure window often considered at 30 to 90 days. Impact, capacity, dependencies, reporter needs, and active exploitation can change the sequence or timing.

        
No funded bounty or guaranteed CVE
There is no funded bug-bounty program and no promise of payment, reward, public acknowledgment, or permanent credit. One Link does not claim CNA status and cannot assign or guarantee a CVE. For an apparently qualifying finding, contributors may help submit information to an appropriate CNA or CVE Program intake; assignment and publication are controlled by those third parties. A funded program remains a target contingent on published rules, funding, and legally capable administration; no launch date is promised.

        
Intake severity, not entitlement
The preliminary intake taxonomy is Critical for silent decryption, identity-key recovery, or universal pairing bypass; High for targeted peer attacks, release supply-chain compromise, or a ratchet break; Medium for timing side channels, denial of service, or metadata leakage beyond /transparency/; and Low for hardening or defense-in-depth gaps. It guides prioritization only and creates no response SLA, remediation deadline, bounty amount, safe-harbor guarantee, or CVE entitlement.

        
Safe-harbor intent; not a legal guarantee
Contributors intend to welcome good-faith, authorized, proportionate research on your own devices and accounts and not to initiate claims solely because such research is reported responsibly. That intent is not legal advice, a contract, authorization to access another person's data or systems, or a waiver of law. Project contributors cannot bind hosting providers, users, individual maintainers, rightsholders, law enforcement, or other third parties. Do not exfiltrate, modify, or destroy others' data or degrade service; request written authorization when scope is uncertain. A formal, versioned, legally reviewed safe-harbor policy remains the target.

        
Evidence and track record
The contributor-maintained /audits/ register links published external reports when they exist and records selected internal review notes. It is not guaranteed exhaustive and is not an independent audit, release attestation, response log, or proof that every report was resolved.
